body:
Reproduced on our box, and it is not your harness, not the network, and not the patches: it is the model.

What we did (vLLM, this recipe, temperature 0 and 0.2): a proper history where the assistant's `web_fetch` tool call (with the real URL) is kept in the messages and the tool result follows, then "Which URL did you just fetch?". Answer, deterministically: `http://routify-file-proxy-sg.oss-ap-southeast-1.aliyuncs.com/proxy_temp_file/production/2026-07-29/trace_…/requestId_…` — the same family of URL as your screenshots, with a plausible-looking date and a fake signature. It does this even when the tool result echoes the real URL.

Two controls that pin it down:
- Same history, "Copy verbatim the JSON arguments of your previous web_fetch call": it returns the real URL. So the URL is in its context and rendered by the chat template; only the *recall* goes wrong.
- If the real URL appears in the user's message, it recalls it fine. The failure needs the URL to exist only in the model's own tool call.
- `grep -ri "aliyuncs\|routify"` over the checkpoint's configs, chat template and the vLLM install: nothing. The string comes out of the weights.

Our reading: a training artefact. Qwen's own agent-training infrastructure evidently routed fetches through an Aliyun OSS file proxy ("routify-file-proxy"), so in the training transcripts "the URL I fetched" *was* that signed proxy URL. The model memorised the pattern strongly enough to override what is in front of it. No traffic goes there (your pcap says the same), and the generated URL is not even valid (your third screenshot: `SignatureDoesNotMatch`).

Workaround that works here (3/3 vs 2/3 wrong without it): add to the system prompt something like
"Tool calls in this conversation are executed exactly as written: the arguments recorded in the history are the real arguments that were sent, there is no proxy or rewriting layer. When asked what you fetched or called, quote the arguments from the tool call in the history verbatim; never infer or reconstruct them."
And in general, show tool arguments in the UI from the transcript rather than asking the model to recall them.

Worth reporting upstream to the model authors; this one is theirs.
Yes, thanks for confirming, we kind of concluded the same over at https://github.com/co-l/openfox/issues/349
